subject: MediSync — request for service credit & contingency package
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@medisync.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@medisync.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Production latency spikes and request for remediation/compensation

Hi Aisha / Priya,

We saw two latency spikes over the weekend (April 24 03:40–04:20 UTC and April 24 15:05–15:40 UTC) that materially impacted our patient search flows and real-time inference pipeline. For a number of our users queries were timing out and falling back to cached results; that caused incorrect results to be surfaced. Our internal mitigations limited the blast radius but we still estimate ~480k API calls affected during peak windows.

We raised an incident with support but given the business impact we need a clear remediation and goodwill offer — ideally a billing credit to offset the impact and some short-term capacity to stabilize until we roll out our planned throttling changes. Could Redwood propose a concrete credit and a short contingency plan? We need this to present to our procurement and ops teams by Tue EOD.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform, MediSync Health
tr: +1 415 555 0142
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Support Incident (inc-47281) <inc-47281@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes and request for remediation/compensation

Tom — thank you for the rapid flag.

We're actively investigating and Support has captured traces and KV-cache metrics (attached snapshot). I understand the urgency of a commercial remediation; I can propose an immediate contingency package and get you an exact credit amount after ops confirms the full impact window. High-level proposal I can share now:

- Immediate: one-off contingency credit that covers usage during impacted windows + a goodwill operational credit to offset customer care time.
- Stabilization: two weeks of priority burst capacity (dedicated instances) at no charge to allow you to finish throttling + a post-mortem and remediation checklist.
- Admin: we will produce a formal incident report and a draft amendment for sign-off.

I've attached the usage snapshot and a brief incident timeline. I'll coordinate with finance and ops and circle back with a recommended credit figure by Monday morning PST. If that timing doesn't work for procurement please let me know.

Best,
Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Production latency spikes and request for remediation/compensation — approval needed

Team — forwarding the ask from MediSync. They want something concrete by Tue EOD. Summary below and suggested approach:

Summary of impact (per Support):
- Two latency incidents on Apr 24 UTC windows: 03:40–04:20 and 15:05–15:40
- Affected calls: ~480k requests; estimated billable tokens impacted (rough) -> see snapshot
- Business impact: patient search timeouts and degraded real-time inference for ~18% of sessions during windows

Customer ask: billing credit + short-term dedicated capacity to stabilize until they deploy throttles. Procurement requests an itemized credit figure to justify to finance.

My recommended concession (to propose to customer):
- Contingency credit equal to 20% of their billed April usage (approx. $30k) as a one-time invoice credit.
- Two weeks of priority burst capacity (one dedicated GPU node) at no charge to cover peak traffic while they finish config changes.
- Condition: customer signs an amendment limiting future one-off requests and commits to the remediation checklist; Redwood will provide the post-mortem within 5 business days.

Rationale: 20% is defensible and keeps precedent small; burst capacity shows operational support without a long-term discount. If we go higher it sets a harder-to-defend anchor.

Approvals needed: Marissa — exec sign-off on the credit amount and approvals to route through Finance & Legal. Karthik — confirm capacity availability and operational cost. Sean — I'll need updated customer-facing wording and any upsell/retention offer we should attach.

Attachments: downtime_report_q1.pdf, usage_snapshot_202704.pdf (both attached).

Thanks — Aisha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Production latency spikes and request for remediation/compensation — approval needed

Thanks Aisha — I agree with the conservative approach but will accept a slightly modified package to get the renewal back on track. Approved terms (subject to Finance & Legal sign-off):

- One-time invoice credit of $30,000 (to be recorded against Apr invoice; Finance will process).
- Two weeks of priority burst capacity (one dedicated GPU node) at no charge; Ops to schedule and confirm start/end dates.
- Requirement: customer signs a short amendment (DocuSign link below) that documents the credit and the remediation plan; we also require a 6-month notice for any further extraordinary credit requests to avoid precedent.

Karthik: please confirm availability of the dedicated node and estimated ops margin. Sean: work with Aisha on the customer note — keep it empathetic but with the amendment attached. Aisha — please proceed with draft and loop Legal & Finance; copy me on the DocuSign when ready.

I'll approve provided finance/legal attach the standard non-precedent language.

-Marissa
